pages.summary: Contour lines drawn at their heights, the contour matrix without drawing, and labels on the lines.
body: `contour3` draws the contour lines of a matrix at their own heights in 3-D. `contourc` computes them without drawing: a matrix of segments, each a column [level; number of points] followed by the points' columns [x; y]. `clabel` writes each line's value on it, given the contour matrix and the contour object that `contour` returns.

examples.title: A hill's contours, flat and in 3-D

pages.summary: Contours of a function of two variables, drawn over a range.
body: `fcontour` evaluates a function handle f(x, y) (written for arrays) over [-5 5] in each direction unless given and draws its contours. `ezcontour` and `ezcontourf` are older forms that also take text such as `'x*exp(-x^2 - y^2)'`, over [-2*pi, 2*pi] unless given, titled with the function; `ezcontourf` fills between the lines.
syntax: The older form, n points a side.

examples.title: One function three ways
examples.code:
f = @(x, y) x.*exp(-x.^2 - y.^2);
subplot(1, 3, 1), fcontour(f, [-2 2 -2 2]), axis equal
subplot(1, 3, 2), ezcontour('x*exp(-x^2 - y^2)', [-2 2 -2 2], 40), axis equal
subplot(1, 3, 3), ezcontourf('x*exp(-x^2 - y^2)', [-2 2 -2 2], 40), axis equal

pages.summary: Surfaces and meshes with more: contours under them, a curtain round the edges, a row of curtains, and lighting.
body: `surfc` and `meshc` draw a surface or a mesh with its contour lines on the floor below. `meshz` hangs a curtain from the mesh's edges down to the lowest value; `waterfall` draws each row of the matrix as a curtain of its own, like a row of profiles. `surfl` draws a surface lit from a light behind the viewer, coloured by how much light each face catches.

examples.title: One surface five ways
examples.code:
[X, Y, Z] = peaks(25);
subplot(2, 3, 1), surfc(X, Y, Z), title('surfc')
subplot(2, 3, 2), meshc(X, Y, Z), title('meshc')
subplot(2, 3, 3), meshz(X, Y, Z), title('meshz')
subplot(2, 3, 4), waterfall(X, Y, Z), title('waterfall')
subplot(2, 3, 5), surfl(X, Y, Z), shading interp, title('surfl')

pages.summary: A pseudocolour plot, and a surface added to the axes without clearing them.
body: `pcolor` draws a matrix as a flat surface seen from above, each cell coloured by the value at its corner (so the last row and column set no cell's colour unless shading is interpolated). `surface` adds a surface object to the current axes as they are, without clearing them or changing the view, and takes its properties by name.

examples.title: A field on a curved grid, and a surface added

pages.summary: Surfaces and meshes of a function of two variables.
body: `fmesh` evaluates a function handle f(x, y) over [-5 5] in each direction unless given and draws a mesh. The older `ezsurf`, `ezmesh`, `ezsurfc` and `ezmeshc` also take text such as `'sin(x)*cos(y)'` (its variables in alphabetical order), over [-2*pi, 2*pi] on a 60-by-60 grid unless given, titled with the function; the c forms add contours below.

examples.title: A ripple
examples.code:
subplot(1, 2, 1), fmesh(@(x, y) sin(x).*cos(y), [-3 3 -3 3])
subplot(1, 2, 2), ezsurfc('sin(x)*cos(y)', [-3 3 -3 3], 30)

pages.summary: Surfaces to try things with: a function with peaks and valleys, a sphere, a cylinder of any profile, an ellipsoid.
body: `peaks` gives a smooth function of two variables with three peaks and two valleys on [-3, 3] (49 points a side unless given). `sphere`, `cylinder` and `ellipsoid` give the coordinates of their surfaces for `surf` or `mesh`, or draw them when no output is asked for; `cylinder` takes a radius profile from bottom to top, so a vector of radii makes a surface of revolution.
syntax: [X, Y, Z] = ellipsoid(xc, yc, zc, xr, yr, zr, n)

examples.title: Four shapes

pages.summary: How surfaces look: flat or smooth colour, lights, and how lit faces are shaded.
body: `shading` sets how surfaces in the axes are coloured: `faceted` (flat with black edges, the default), `flat` (no edges) or `interp` (colours blended across each face). `light` adds a light at a position and `camlight` one near the camera; `lighting` then shades lit faces `flat` or `gouraud` (smooth), or turns lighting off with `none`. `material` sets how the surfaces and patches reflect light (`shiny`, `dull`, `metal`, or the strengths as numbers): their reflectance properties, which the page keeps but does not draw.

examples.title: One sphere three ways
examples.code:
[x, y, z] = sphere(30);
subplot(1, 3, 1), surf(x, y, z), axis equal, title('faceted')
subplot(1, 3, 2), surf(x, y, z), shading interp, axis equal, title('interp')
subplot(1, 3, 3), surf(x, y, z, 'FaceColor', [0.8 0.5 0.2], 'EdgeColor', 'none'), axis equal
camlight headlight, lighting gouraud, title('lit')

pages.summary: The limits of the colour scale, and two older settings that are accepted.
body: `clim` sets the values that map to the first and last colours of the colormap (values beyond take the end colours), or gives them; `clim auto` lets the data set them again. `caxis` is its older name. `alpha` and `hidden` are accepted and have no effect: transparency is set by an object's FaceAlpha, and meshes are drawn with hidden lines removed.

examples.title: The same data on two scales
examples.code:
Z = peaks(30);
subplot(1, 2, 1), imagesc(Z), colorbar, axis image
clim
subplot(1, 2, 2), imagesc(Z), colorbar, axis image
clim([-2 2])

pages.summary: The camera: zoom by a factor, its view angle, and pointing it at objects.
body: The axes are drawn as a camera sees them, from a position toward a target, with a view angle: the smaller the angle, the larger the axes. `camzoom` narrows the angle by a factor (above 1 nearer, below 1 farther); `camva` sets or gives the angle itself. `camlookat` points the camera at objects and closes in until they fill the view.

examples.title: Half as near again
examples.code:
[x, y, z] = sphere(16);
surf(x, y, z), axis equal
va = camva
camzoom(1.5)
camva

examples.title: At the last of three spheres
examples.code:
[x, y, z] = sphere(16);
hold on
for k = 0:2
    h(k + 1) = surf(x + 3*k, y, z);
end
hold off, axis equal, view(3)
camlookat(h(3))
camva
